Rishi / Neha — internal notes from the competitive evaluation perspective and suggested test matrix to validate incident response claims for ACME: 

Summary comparisons (high-level):
- Redwood: 24/7 on-call rotation, target RCA draft within 72 hours for Sev1, formal RCA & remediation plan within 7 days; SLA crediting tiers defined by incident duration (we can be explicit once legal weighs in). Supports automatic routing to warm standby replicas and transparent model variant fallback (configurable).
- Hyperscaler A: 24/7 support but RCA timelines often longer (5–10 days for complex infra incidents); credit model generally managed via cloud credits and can be slower to disburse.
- Other inference API: variable — some smaller providers rely on manual failover and have less formal RCA SLAs.

Suggested acceptance tests (proposed):
1) Failover test: induce a node-level failure for 30m — measure failover time, 95/99/99.9 latency during event, and success rate.
2) Traffic spike + degraded model variant: simulate 3x traffic with small model fallback — validate quality delta and throttling behavior.
3) RCA turnaround simulation: submit a synthetic Sev1 and validate initial acknowledgement, timeline to substantive RCA (expectation: initial ack < 1h, investigation summary < 24h, draft RCA < 72h).
4) Escalation chain verification: ensure named points (on-call, manager, exec escalation) are reachable and response SLAs met.

Please confirm that we can publish the above as the test plan to Acme (I’ll draft the test plan doc). I recommend we propose a maintenance window the week of Nov 9–13.

--
Marissa Cole
